title: Client slice negotiation and tool SLA proposal
body:
Executive summary:

This is a working PRD sketch for a lightweight "client slice negotiation" mechanism + formalized "tool SLA" concept for the Hosted API. Goal: enable deterministic streaming semantics and predictable tool-calling behavior for latency-sensitive clients (mobile, web micro-interactions) while preserving throughput/cost optimizations in the runtime.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Customers want low-latency incremental responses and the ability to call external tools (search, db, code-run) during streaming, without unpredictable tail latency from long tool invocations.
- Current hosted streaming produces opaque partial outputs; SDKs struggle to coordinate prefetch vs. synchronous tool calls, leading to client-side complexity and retries.
- We need a minimal contract so the server, SDK, and client app can negotiate priorities and fallback behavior rather than ad-hoc timeouts.

Scope / non-goals:
- In scope: handshake at call start to declare latency budgets, prefetch lanes, and tool SLAs; streaming markers to indicate tool blocking vs. non-blocking frames; SDK ergonomic surfaces to express preferred fallbacks and prefetch hints.
- Out of scope: full orchestrator redesign, mandatory client-side caching semantics, or new billing models (billing follow-on).

Success metrics (90-day / long):
- 90-day: developer friction reduced — integrate sample app using SDK prefetch lanes in <2 hours; observed 30% fewer client retries in lab tests.
- 6-month: 20% reduction in median tool-call-triggered tail latency for streaming sessions in production experiments; telemetry shows correct handshake usage for >70% of active clients using the new SDK surface.

User stories:
- As a mobile app engineer I want to tell the API that the current session has a 300ms latency budget so the server prioritizes partial token returns and defers non-critical tool calls.
- As an ML product owner I want tool calls that exceed their SLA to be auto-fallbacked to cached responses or lightweight model-only substitutes so user experience is preserved.
- As an SDK maintainer I want a small, composable API that exposes negotiation, tool call annotations, and structured-output hooks without forcing complex state machines on clients.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Call-time negotiation headers / handshake
   - client-slice: JSON-lite string (small) declaring desired lanes and budgets. Example lanes: "fast": 200ms, "interactive": 500ms, "batch": 2000ms.
   - tool-sla-hint: per-tool preferred max latency and fallback policy id (e.g., fallback=cached|model|deferred).
   - server returns accepted-slice header confirming effective budgets (may be tightened).

2) Streaming frames & tool markers
   - Introduce explicit frame types in streaming output: partial-text, tool-materialize, tool-blocked, tool-fallback, final.
   - tool-blocked frames indicate the server has issued a tool call that is still pending; clients can surface a lightweight UI indicator.
   - tool-materialize frames carry structured tool results (JSON payloads) and a tool-provenance tag.

3) Tool SLA enforcement & fallback behavior
   - Each tool invocation carries an effective SLA (from negotiation). If the tool does not respond within SLA, runtime can apply configured fallback: return cached result, return model-synthesized best-effort, or continue without tool result and mark with tool-fallback.
   - Fallback policy defined in config: DESC order of preference; policies stored and versioned in the control plane.

4) Structured output and schema versioning
   - Structured tool outputs must be wrapped in a small envelope: {"tool": "search.v1","result": ..., "confidence": 0.82, "schema_version": "2025-01-1"}.
   - SDKs must expose typed parsers; server will emit a schema id and a human-readable contract link in the frame.

5) SDK ergonomics (minimal surfaces)
   - JS / Python SDK add-on: pass negotiation args when creating a streaming call, e.g. // pseudocode
     client.stream({ prompt, slices: [{name:'fast',budgetMs:200}], toolHints: [{name:'search',maxMs:80,fallback:'cached'}] })
   - Callbacks: onPartial(textFrame, metadata), onToolPending(toolMeta), onToolResult(toolResult), onFallback(toolMeta, reason).
   - High-level helper: client.streamWithGrace({ prompt, interactiveBudget:300, fallthroughPolicy: 'model' }) to cover common mobile use-cases.

Operational considerations:
- Control plane needs to support fallback policy definitions and per-tenant defaults.
- Runtime needs lightweight timer hooks to enforce tool SLAs and produce tool-blocked/tool-fallback frames without blocking token emission.
- Cache integration: prefer cache lookups for high-frequency tool calls; cache consistency rules should be documented separately.

Telemetry & observability:
- Emit the following per request: negotiatedSlice, per-tool effectiveSLAMs, toolStart/timeToFirstByte, toolFallbackReason, overall latency percentiles by slice.
- Console: add per-route "tool-fallback rate" and "slice acceptance" dashboard.

Backward compatibility & migration:
- Default: no change for older SDKs. Server will not emit tool-blocked frames unless negotiation occurs.
- SDK opt-in: new SDK versions pass negotiation headers by default when using streaming APIs.

Security & safety notes:
- Tool materialize frames must be sanitized and limited (size budget) to prevent large payloads streaming into clients.
- Tool provenance tags required for audit and tracing; tie to request-level correlation ids.

Rollout plan (phased):
1) Internal lab (2 weeks): implement handshake parsing, test harness for synthetic tool delays and fallback modes.
2) Canary: expose to 5% of hosted-api routes for customers that opt-in (feature flag). Collect metrics and SDK integration feedback (6 weeks).
3) Gradual rollout with configurable tenant defaults and docs (3 months).

Open questions / tradeoffs (working):
- Should server pick a default fallback per tool globally, or is tenant-level control required? (leaning tenant-level)
- How to surface partial materialized tool outputs for privacy-sensitive data? Add per-tool redaction flags?
- Do we need a token-level billing distinction for tool-materialize frames (likely yes; billing design later).

Implementation notes (engineering checklist):
- [ ] wire client-specified headers through gateway -> control plane -> runtime
- [ ] implement server-side timer enforcement in runtime
- [ ] add streaming frame types and wire them through socket/HTTP chunking
- [ ] SDK: add JS + Python negotiation args + callback surfaces
- [ ] observability: instrument tool SLA enforcement events
- [ ] doc: developer integration guide + sample mobile app demo

Appendix: sample handshake header (compact string)
client-slice: "fast:200,interactive:500"
client-tool-hints: "search:max=80,fallback=cached;db:max=250,fallback=deferred"

Sample streaming exchange (toy):
- server: partial-text("Looking up docs...")
- server: tool-blocked(tool=search, id=abc123)
- server: partial-text("While we fetch, here’s a quick summary...")
- runtime: tool-materialize(tool=search, id=abc123, payload={...})
- server: final("Final answer with embedded citation [search:abc123]")

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: keep the handshake compact, favor SDK helpers for developer ergonomics, and enforce SLAs in the runtime rather than complicating the client.
- Feedback wanted on: preferred SLA field names, whether to allow negative acknowledgements (server can reject slice with reason), and if we should expose per-tool cost estimates in negotiation.

-- end --
